transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Tran (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM); Dana Rogers, Maya Singh, Carlos Duarte, Leah Kim (Clarity Health)

[00:00] Sofia Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, this is Sofia from Redwood. Evan's our solutions engineer, Priya's on customer success, and from Clarity you are Dana and Maya and team. quick round robin?
[00:15] Dana Rogers: yeah hi thanks, Dana here head of ML at Clarity. excited to get started, we wanna reduce inference latency for our triage assistant and also lock down security controls.
[00:30] Maya Singh: Maya here, CTO. main ask is predictable costs and an easy path to private deployment if needed.
[00:45] Carlos Duarte: Carlos, infra lead — we'll handle network and cloud setup.
[00:50] Leah Kim: Leah product, coordinating success metrics.
[00:55] Sofia Patel: awesome. agenda: goals, architecture options, security checklist, pilot scope, timeline and next steps. any additions?
[01:05] Maya Singh: no that's good. maybe also a quick note on how rollouts work for model versions and canaries.
[01:12] Evan Tran: sure we can cover that briefly. so to frame it, teams usually start with a hosted API for quick tests, then a dedicated reserved pool when throughput and predictability matter, and private (VPC/on-prem) when data residency and network controls are required.
[01:30] Dana Rogers: we are leaning toward Dedicated initially then evaluate Private. main constraints: PHI-ish data, need audit logs and KMS integration, and also want sub-150ms median token latency for 512 token requests.
[01:45] Evan Tran: ok that helps. for Dedicated we can provide reserved GPU pools, autoscale policies, and we support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping when in Private. for hosted we have envelope encryption but for HIPAA-ish scenarios we usually recommend Dedicated or Private.
[02:10] Carlos Duarte: how does VPC peering look — do you support cross-account VPC peering or require transit? any IP whitelisting?
[02:20] Evan Tran: we do VPC peering for Redwood Private: customers create a peering connection to our control plane endpoints, and for Dedicated we offer secure peering to the GPU pool. we also support IP allow lists and private endpoints. i'll share a network diagram in the runbook.
[02:42] Dana Rogers: perfect, also curious about kms: can we use our AWS KMS keys or do you need keys in your account?
[02:50] Priya Kapoor: short answer, if you're on Private you can bring your KMS keys (CMKs). for Dedicated we offer options: customer-managed keys via KMS in customer's account with key grants, or Redwood-managed keys with strict controls. we'll put the exact flow in the security doc.
[03:10] Maya Singh: SOC2 and audit logs — do you provide tenant-level logging and export to our SIEM?
[03:18] Evan Tran: yes we have audit logs and can stream events to your SIEM (S3/Kinesis/Cloudwatch). logs include token-level metadata, call traces and model version details. there's an add-on for extended retention.
[03:30] Leah Kim: success metrics — we want to measure latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, and false-positive rates on the triage classifier. pilot should define targets.
[03:42] Sofia Patel: noted. typical pilot we run is 2 weeks: week 1 baseline with sample traffic and baseline model (hosted or dedicated), week 2 optimizations — batching, kv caching, quantization recommendations, and then a benchmark report. does that timeline work?
[03:58] Dana Rogers: two weeks sounds ok but we may need a little prep time to sanitize data. can we schedule the benchmark window the week of Aug 24?
[04:05] Priya Kapoor: yes we can do Aug 24. Evan will run the benchmark harness and share a spreadsheet.
[04:12] Carlos Duarte: what about ingress egress costs? if we peer via VPC and traffic stays in-region, are there extra egress charges?
[04:22] Evan Tran: with private peering typically inter-region/pricing depends on cloud provider. we'll include an estimated cost breakdown in the pilot pricing doc; for Dedicated we can give unit economics per token.
[04:35] Maya Singh: okay, on the integration side we plan to use your HTTP API from our inference orchestrator. do you have SDKs and examples for node/python? and telemetry hooks?
[04:45] Evan Tran: yes, SDKs for python/node/go, and we provide tracing hooks and per-request metadata for tracing. we'll share a sample integration repo link.
[04:58] Dana Rogers: about model versions and rollouts: we need canary testing and automatic rollback if quality drifts. how mature is that?
[05:06] Evan Tran: rollouts are supported in the console — canary percentages, A/B, automatic fallback to a previous pinned version on error rates. quality regression detection is part of Redwood Optimize if you want automated alerts tied to prompt sets.
[05:22] Leah Kim: that sounds useful. what's the uplift to add Optimize?
[05:27] Sofia Patel: it's an add-on, we'll include pricing options in the pilot proposal.
[05:35] Maya Singh: any gotchas on model quantization and accuracy tradeoffs? we need guidance before we flip any bits into production.
[05:43] Evan Tran: yes quantization can reduce memory and increase speed but may slightly affect per-token quality. we'll run suggested quant profiles against your eval prompts in week 2 and show quality metrics. usually we recommend int8/4 profiles for throughput-heavy endpoints.
[06:00] Dana Rogers: for the triage assistant our acceptable drift threshold is <2% drop in precision on the key intents.
[06:07] Evan Tran: noted, we'll include those thresholds in the benchmark and the report.
[06:15] Sofia Patel: quick note on compliance docs: we'll share SOC2 summary, pen test summary, and our private deploy checklist.
[06:23] Maya Singh: great, also send over any contract terms for data handling.
[06:27] Sofia Patel: will do.
[06:30] Dana Rogers: one small ask — can we get a small sample of latency numbers for a comparable customer (same model size, similar token lengths)? ballpark is fine.
[06:38] Evan Tran: sure i can share anonymized bench numbers. typical p50 for a 7B model on Dedicated is 40–80ms per token depending on sequence length and batching; we'll include ranges in the doc.
[06:52] Leah Kim: thanks.
[06:55] Sofia Patel: ok wrapping up, let's recap next steps and owners.
[07:00] Priya Kapoor: recap: Evan to share runbook, network diagram, sample integration repo and anonymized benchmarks; Sofia to send pilot pricing and SLA summary; Dana to send sample traffic/profile and datasets; Priya to schedule weekly check-ins starting Aug 24.
[07:18] Maya Singh: sounds good.
[07:20] Carlos Duarte: quick question — do you support private connectors for on-prem model hosting?
[07:25] Evan Tran: yes we have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments, that's typically a later-phase engagement.
[07:32] Dana Rogers: ok thanks everyone.
[07:34] Sofia Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up with the runbook and calendar invites.
[07:38] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription contains minor speaker attribution errors and occasional dropped words; timestamps are approximate. References shared: onboarding runbook (link to be provided), pilot benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared by Evan).

End of transcript.
